lead.headline: PINK LINE SET FOR NOVEMBER 13 OPENING, TAKING METRO PAST 100 KM
lead.deck: The 7.5-km elevated stretch will serve six stations; residents are urging an earlier start after years of delay
paragraphs: The Prime Minister’s Office has confirmed November 13 as the inauguration date for the elevated section of Bengaluru’s Namma Metro Pink Line, a Karnataka official said. The first phase covers 7.5 km and six stations between Kalena Agrahara and Tavarekere.

The Commissioner for Metro Railway Safety cleared the stretch last week. Chief Minister D K Shivakumar said Prime Minister Narendra Modi would travel from Tavarekere to IIMB-Bilekahalli and launch services.
When it opens, the addition will take Bengaluru Metro’s operational network to 103.6 km. Residents have called for the cleared line to open sooner instead of waiting for the scheduled ceremony.

sidebarStory.headline: MEA REPORTS 23 INDIAN DEATHS IN WEST ASIA CONFLICT
sidebarStory.subhead: The toll includes 15 seafarers; five more Indians have died in Black Sea shipping attacks
paragraphs: The Ministry of External Affairs said 23 Indian nationals, including 15 seafarers, have died in the West Asia conflict. Five more Indians have died in attacks on commercial shipping in the Black Sea. After a ship was attacked off Oman, 13 crew members were rescued and repatriation arrangements are under way.

stories.headline: SOUTH CITY CORPORATION SEALS 63 UNLICENSED SHOPS
stories.deck: Most of the affected units were in BTM Layout residential areas
paragraphs: Bengaluru South City Corporation sealed 63 commercial units operating without trade licences in residential areas on roads narrower than 40 feet. The action covered businesses including food outlets, salons and retail shops, with the largest number reported in BTM Layout.

stories.headline: AIRPORT ROAD JUNCTIONS GET PEDESTRIAN SAFETY UPGRADES
paragraphs: NHAI has added marked crossings, refuge islands, guard rails and improved footpaths at Byatarayanapura and Kodigehalli on Ballari Road. About 80% of work at those two junctions is complete; Jakkur work is planned later because Metro construction is under way.

stories.headline: ADVOCATES BOYCOTT COURTS, SEEK STRONGER PROTECTION
paragraphs: Lawyers in Bengaluru joined a statewide court boycott on November 3 after attacks on advocates, demanding stronger safeguards and implementation of the state’s protection law. Association representatives raised their concerns before a Karnataka High Court bench.

stories.headline: MURASU’S AFTERMATH: RELIEF CENTRES OPEN AS HEAVY RAIN CONTINUES
stories.deck: The storm damaged crops and homes; authorities kept evacuations and school closures in place
paragraphs: Murasu weakened into a cyclonic storm over South Coastal Andhra Pradesh on Tuesday. Authorities reported two deaths and placed more than 12,000 people in rehabilitation centres as rain and flooding affected coastal districts.
Preliminary estimates put damage at ₹344 crore, with crops across 52,459 hectares affected and 312 houses damaged. Andhra Pradesh and Odisha continued relief operations and precautionary closures.

stories.headline: INDIA BUSINESS CONFIDENCE INDEX RISES 8.12% IN OCTOBER
paragraphs: The Assocham Business Confidence Index rose to 128.72 in October from 119.05 a year earlier, IANS reported. Assocham attributed the rise to GST collections, bank credit growth, passenger-vehicle sales, sustained purchasing managers' index expansion and feedback on economic reforms.

stories.headline: DISTRICT PEACE COMMITTEES FORMED ACROSS ALL 16 MANIPUR DISTRICTS
paragraphs: Manipur has ordered an 11-member peace committee in each district, led by the district magistrate and including police, officials and community representatives. The bodies are tasked with dialogue, addressing grievances and identifying tensions early; they are to meet at least once every two weeks.

groups.ariaLabel: Karnataka and India farmers, law, and industry news

stories.headline: STATE SEEKS ₹22,400 CRORE FROM CENTRE FOR DROUGHT LOSSES
stories.deck: The revised claim cites crop damage across 57.93 lakh hectares in 226 taluks
paragraphs: Karnataka Deputy Chief Minister G Parameshwara has urged the Centre to approve and release ₹22,400.58 crore in drought assistance. The revised memorandum estimates losses of ₹62,481.88 crore, with crops damaged across 57.93 lakh hectares in 226 taluks.
Parameshwara says current relief rates do not reflect cultivation costs and asked the Centre to use updated farmer records when identifying eligible beneficiaries.

stories.headline: FOREIGN DIVORCE DECREE CANNOT SHIELD MAN FROM BIGAMY CASE: SC
paragraphs: The Supreme Court declined to quash bigamy proceedings against a man who relied on a UK divorce decree based on irretrievable breakdown of marriage. The bench said that decree could not bind his first wife, who had not submitted to the foreign court’s jurisdiction, or override Indian matrimonial law.

stories.headline: RAJNATH SETS ₹3-LAKH-CRORE DEFENCE PRODUCTION TARGET FOR 2029
paragraphs: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh reiterated targets of ₹3 lakh crore in domestic defence production and ₹50,000 crore in exports by 2029. He said production reached about ₹1.78 lakh crore in 2025–26 and called for more home-grown research, manufacturing and technology partnerships.

stories.headline: INDIA OPEN FIVE-MATCH ODI TOUR AGAINST NEW ZEALAND TODAY
stories.deck: The first match is at Eden Park in Auckland as India begin their 2026–27 away series
paragraphs: India meet New Zealand in the first ODI at Auckland’s Eden Park on Wednesday, November 4. The match begins at 2:00 am UTC (7:30 am IST), according to the BCCI fixture; four more ODIs follow in the series.

stories.headline: IMD FORECASTS SHOWERS AND THUNDERSTORMS TODAY
paragraphs: The IMD forecast partly cloudy skies with one or two spells of rain or thundershowers in Bengaluru on November 4, with a minimum of 20°C and maximum of 30°C. Thunderstorms accompanied by lightning are also forecast.
